Process MIC values and assign interpretive phenotypes by genus

Source: R/process_mic_values_function.R
process_mic_values.Rd

This function takes a data frame containing MIC measurements and assigns interpretive phenotypes ("Susceptible" or "Resistant") based on predefined genus-specific lookup tables. MIC values are first recategorized into discrete bins based on the specified maximum MIC threshold.

Usage

process_mic_values(df, max_mic = 256)

Arguments

df

A data frame with the following columns: measurement_value, accession, new_genus, and optionally phenotype.

max_mic

Numeric value defining the upper MIC threshold. Supported values: 64, 256, 1024.

Value

A data frame with original columns plus:

  • recategorized_mic: discretized MIC values based on bin configuration.

  • phenotype_assigned: interpretive phenotype inferred by genus, or fallback to original phenotype.

Examples

mic_sample <- data.frame(
  accession = c("SRR000001", "SRR000002", "SRR000003"),
  measurement_value = c(4, 32, 128),
  new_genus = c("Escherichia", "Klebsiella", "Pseudomonas"),
  phenotype = c("Resistant", NA, "Intermediate"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
result <- process_mic_values(mic_sample, max_mic = 256)
head(result)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   accession measurement_value new_genus   phenotype    recategorized_mic
#>   <chr>                 <dbl> <chr>       <chr>        <fct>            
#> 1 SRR000001                 4 Escherichia Resistant    4                
#> 2 SRR000002                32 Klebsiella  NA           32               
#> 3 SRR000003               128 Pseudomonas Intermediate 128              
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: phenotype_assigned <chr>
